newsitem.title: INDIA: Cyprus president woos Indian exporters, investors.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus president woos Indian exporters, investors.

text.p: Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides on Tuesday urged Indian businessmen to use his country as a bridge to Europe, the Middle East and Africa, and pledged to open his country further to foreign investment.

"Cyprus has the potential to become a cultural, economic and political bridge between East and West," Clerides, who arrived in New Delhi on Monday on a six-day official visit, told a business luncheon.
He was accompanied by his wife, Lilla-Irene, and Foreign Minister Alecos Michaelides.

"Attracting inward investment has always been one of the primary objectives of Cyprus's development policy. The Cyprus government is in the process of liberalising further its investment policy," the president said.
Clerides said most proposals for foreign participation of up to 100 percent in Cyprus would be permitted under the new policy. He did not elaborate.

The president said India and Cyprus had signed a treaty on merchant shipping during his visit. "It is hoped that further agreements on the protection and promotion of investments, and on air transport will soon be concluded," Clerides said.
In 1994 the two nations signed a double-taxation avoidance pact that offered attractive tax concessions to Indian investors in the Mediterranean island, he said.
The president said Cyprus would consider setting up duty-free bonded warehouses for Indian goods destined for export to European Union member countries.
A delegation from the Cyprus Chamber of Commerce was scheduled to visit India later this year, he said.

Clerides said Cyprus offered significant opportunities to Indian businessmen in shipping and the offshore sector, where tax rates were favourable. The Mediterranean island is among the world's top five maritime nations.
Cyprus possesses a highly developed economy that meets the European Union's criteria for economic and monetary union, Clerides said.

"Despite the progress we have achieved in the economic field, however, the full realisation of the potential of Cyprus is hampered by the division of my country as a result of the Turkish invasion and the continuing occupation of 37 percent of its territory," the president said.
The island has been divided since Turkey invaded the north in 1974 after a Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia engineered by the military then in power in Greece.
Decades of international efforts to reunite the island under a federal umbrella have failed and the dispute remains a source of tension between NATO partners Greece and Turkey.
